SMTO-TSK-0025 — A queued task is linked to a different request

GUID: 353996e6-acb7-4f18-a2dc-dba154f21422
Slug: queue-binding-conflict
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • Each queued task is tied to one saved request and the task before it. This one no longer matches, often because the queue changed in another tab. The task may already have started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close any other SMTO tabs showing this conversation, then reload this page. Changes to the queue in another tab are a common reason the saved link no longer matches.
  2. Look in the conversation for a reply to this queued task, and check whether it is still in the Queued list above the message box. The task may already be running or finished, and adding it again would do the work twice.
  3. Only if it has neither started nor stayed in the Queued list, type the request again and queue it as a new task. A new queued task gets its own fresh link, so it can't clash with the old one.

What success looks like

  • The queued task appears once, either in the Queued list or as a reply in the conversation, and runs in order.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resubmitting the same queued item.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A queue submission was refused because its queue ID, prepared request, predecessor lineage, submission identity or digest differs from the durable binding (or the binding is missing or cannot be verified).

What this means

  • Queue ID, prepared request, predecessor lineage, submission digest or conversation deletion fence differs from the durable binding. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Queue ID, prepared request, predecessor lineage, submission digest or conversation deletion fence differs from the durable binding.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact durable queue/request/predecessor bindings and any deletion fence, preserving already accepted identities.

How to fix it

  • Compare the queue_id, prepared_request_id, predecessor_request_id and snapshot digest in the request with the queue_submissions binding. Reload the queue and reconnect to the request already bound to this item; check its run status before creating any different work, and never reuse or alter an existing submission identity.
  • Refresh the queue and reconnect to the existing request bound to this item. Reconcile its current status before creating different work; do not reuse or alter durable submission identities.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The client reconnects to the correct existing submission or creates distinct new work only after reconciliation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
